questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = 5\cos(4x)$ is shown for $0 \le x \le \pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.2, xmax=3.5, ymin=-6.2, ymax=6.2,
  xtick={0.7854, 1.5708, 2.3562, 3.1416},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{4}$, $\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\frac{3\pi}{4}$, $\pi$},
  ytick={-5, 5},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:3.1416] {5*cos(deg(4*x))};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
What is the period of this function?

options.why: Multiplied $2\pi$ by the horizontal dilation constant instead of dividing by it.
Used the amplitude $5$ as the horizontal dilation constant in $\frac{2\pi}{a}$.
Applied the tangent period $\frac{\pi}{a}$ instead of the cosine period $\frac{2\pi}{a}$.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = -3\sin x + 2$ is shown for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.3, xmax=6.9, ymin=-2.4, ymax=6.4,
  xtick={1.5708, 3.1416, 4.7124, 6.2832},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$},
  ytick={-1, 2, 5},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:6.2832] {-3*sin(deg(x))+2};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
What is the range of this function?

options.why: Applied the reflection to the vertical translation as well, giving a mean position of $-2$.
Added the amplitude to the mean position but did not subtract it, keeping only the upper half.
Used the amplitude alone and ignored the vertical translation of $2$.

questions.solution_text:
$y = -3\sin x + 2$ has amplitude $|-3| = 3$ and mean position $y=2$.
Range $=[2-3,\ 2+3]$
$=[-1, 5]$

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = \cos\left(3x+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is shown for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.3, xmax=6.9, ymin=-1.6, ymax=1.6,
  xtick={1.5708, 3.1416, 4.7124, 6.2832},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$},
  ytick={-1, 1},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:6.2832] {cos(deg(3*x+pi/2))};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
This curve is the graph of $y = \cos(3x)$ after which horizontal translation?

options.why: Factorised correctly but read $+\frac{\pi}{6}$ inside the bracket as a shift to the right.
Read the translation straight off $+\frac{\pi}{2}$ without factorising the $3$ out of the bracket.
Did not factorise the $3$ out and also reversed the direction of the shift.

questions.solution_text:
$y = \cos\left(3x+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$
$= \cos\left(3\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)$
A $+\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ inside the bracket shifts the curve $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ to the left.

questions.question_text:
The graph below has the form $y = k\sin(ax)$ with $k>0$ and $a>0$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.6, xmax=13.6, ymin=-8, ymax=8,
  xtick={3.1416, 6.2832, 9.4248, 12.5664},
  xticklabels={$\pi$, $2\pi$, $3\pi$, $4\pi$},
  ytick={-6, 6},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:12.5664] {6*sin(deg(x/2))};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
What is the equation of this curve?

options.why: Inverted the horizontal dilation, reading a period of $4\pi$ as $a=2$ rather than $a=\frac{1}{2}$.
Used the full distance from minimum to maximum as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Used the maximum-to-minimum distance as the amplitude and also inverted the horizontal dilation.

questions.solution_text:
The curve runs between $y=-6$ and $y=6$, so the amplitude is $6$.
$k = 6$
One complete cycle runs from $x=0$ to $x=4\pi$, so the period is $4\pi$.
$\dfrac{2\pi}{a} = 4\pi$
$a = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$y = 6\sin\dfrac{x}{2}$

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = 2\cos(3x)-5$ is shown for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.3, xmax=6.9, ymin=-8.4, ymax=1.4,
  xtick={1.5708, 3.1416, 4.7124, 6.2832},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$},
  ytick={-7, -5, -3},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:6.2832] {2*cos(deg(3*x))-5};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
What is the range of this function?

options.why: Took the mean position as $y=5$, using $+5$ instead of $-5$.
Measured the amplitude upward from the mean position only, ignoring the lower half.
Used a mean position of $y=5$ and measured the amplitude upward only.

questions.solution_text:
$y = 2\cos(3x)-5$ has amplitude $2$ and mean position $y=-5$.
Range $=[-5-2,\ -5+2]$
$=[-7, -3]$

options.why: Used the asymptotes of $y=\tan x$ and ignored the horizontal dilation by $3$.
Placed the asymptotes at the $x$-intercepts of the transformed curve instead of the breaks.
Repeated the asymptotes every $\frac{\pi}{6}$, using half the period instead of the full period $\frac{\pi}{3}$.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = 2\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)-4$ is shown for $0 \le x \le 6\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.8, xmax=20, ymin=-7.2, ymax=1.4,
  xtick={3.1416, 6.2832, 9.4248, 12.5664, 15.7080, 18.8496},
  xticklabels={$\pi$, $2\pi$, $3\pi$, $4\pi$, $5\pi$, $6\pi$},
  ytick={-6, -4, -2},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:18.8496] {2*sin(deg(x/3))-4};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which sequence of transformations takes $y = \sin x$ to this curve?

options.text: Dilate vertically by a factor of $2$, dilate horizontally by a factor of $3$, then translate $4$ units down.
Dilate vertically by a factor of $2$, dilate horizontally by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{3}$, then translate $4$ units down.
options.why: Inverted the horizontal dilation factor, reading $\sin\frac{x}{3}$ as a compression rather than a stretch.

options.text: Dilate vertically by a factor of $2$, dilate horizontally by a factor of $3$, then translate $4$ units up.
options.why: Read the $-4$ as an upward translation instead of a downward one.

options.text: Dilate vertically by a factor of $2$, dilate horizontally by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{3}$, then translate $4$ units up.
options.why: Inverted the horizontal dilation factor and also reversed the direction of the vertical translation.

questions.solution_text:
$y = 2\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)-4$ has $k=2$, $a=\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $c=-4$.
A horizontal dilation constant of $a=\dfrac{1}{3}$ is a stretch by a factor of $3$, since the period becomes $6\pi$.
Dilate vertically by a factor of $2$, dilate horizontally by a factor of $3$, then translate $4$ units down.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $g(x) = 1-4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{6}\right)$ is shown for $0 \le x \le 24$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-1, xmax=26, ymin=-4.6, ymax=6.4,
  xtick={6, 12, 18, 24},
  ytick={-3, 1, 5},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:24] {1-4*cos(deg(pi*x/6))};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
What are the period and the maximum value of $g(x)$?

options.why: Took the amplitude $4$ as the maximum value, ignoring the vertical translation of $1$.
Divided $2\pi$ by $6$ instead of by the horizontal dilation constant $\frac{\pi}{6}$.
Divided $2\pi$ by $6$ and also used the amplitude alone as the maximum.

questions.solution_text:
$g(x) = -4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{6}\right)+1$ has $a=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, amplitude $4$ and mean position $y=1$.
Period $=\dfrac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{6}}$
$=12$
Maximum $=1+4$
$=5$

questions.question_text: Given that $f(x)=5\sin(4\pi x)$, find the period of $f$.

options.why: Uses the coefficient without cancelling the pi in the period formula.
Multiplies by the angular frequency instead of taking its reciprocal.
Ignores the factor of pi when calculating the period.

questions.solution_text: For $a\sin(bx)$, the period is $\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$. Here $b=4\pi$, so the period is $\frac{2\pi}{4\pi}=\frac12$.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum value of $4\cos(x-\frac{\pi}{3})+6$?

options.why: Uses the maximum value of cosine rather than its minimum.
Does not apply the amplitude and vertical translation correctly.
Subtracts one from the constant without multiplying by the amplitude 4.

questions.solution_text: The minimum of cosine is -1, so the minimum value is $4(-1)+6=2$.
